_comment: MCP resource spec for #6 AI Eval Coverage Scorecard. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Draft 2026-05-17 — owner to validate.

resource.name: AI Eval Coverage Scorecard
resource.description: Describe an AI feature in three sentences. Returns coverage status across seven eval categories (correctness, refusal, latency, hallucination, jailbreak, regression, drift) with starter eval prompts for the gaps.

tools.name: eval_coverage_classify
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Classifies the user's feature description across the seven eval categories. Returns covered/partial/missing per category with one-sentence reasoning.

tools.name: eval_coverage_score
tools.description: Deterministic. Computes the coverage score 0-100 from category classifications.

tools.name: eval_coverage_starter_set
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Generates 2-3 starter eval prompts per missing or partial category. Returns a JSON export ready to ingest into Braintrust, LangSmith, or a plain harness.

tools.name: eval_coverage_portfolio_view
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Aggregates scorecards across multiple features the user has scored. Surfaces patterns ('regression sets missing on 5 of 8 features').
tools._phase_note: Web version does not expose this tool. Portfolio aggregation requires persisted prior scorecards, which is .mcpb data-dir scope.

_open_questions: Validate ui:// URI scheme against current MCP Apps spec.
JSON export format: should the .mcpb version write to ~/.working-from-lenny/evals/<timestamp>.json or prompt the user for a path? Default-on filesystem write is the convention violation to check.
Does the portfolio view need user opt-in, or is local-only aggregation acceptable by default?

Should the seven categories be configurable (user can add 'tone consistency' or 'multi-turn coherence') or locked? Locked is simpler; configurable is more honest about how varied AI features actually are.
_proposed_answers: Confirmed valid. The Jan 2026 MCP Apps spec uses ui:// for embedded UI resources. 'ui://working-from-lenny/eval-coverage' matches the required pattern.

Prompt for path on first use, then remember the last-used path as the default. Default-on silent writes to ~/working-from-lenny/ are the convention violation: the Jan 2026 spec requires tools with fs-write capability to declare that capability in the manifest and either get explicit approval or prompt for path. Prompting once and caching the preference splits the difference: no surprise writes, minimal friction after the first use.

Opt-in, consistent with the plan's privacy posture. Local-only aggregation still creates a persistent record of which features the user has scored and how, which is data they should knowingly retain. Enable via the data-retention capability in the bundle manifest, same pattern as the stateful tools on other apps.

Lock the seven categories for Phase 2. They are corpus-anchored against evals-for-ai-products.md and represent a defensible standard set. Configurable categories complicate the portfolio view: cross-feature comparisons break if categories differ per feature. Add an optional free-text 'notes' field per category as an escape hatch without opening the category list to per-user configuration. Revisit in Phase 3 once real usage shows which categories users most want to extend.
